data.narrative:
Elementary Robotics is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Arye Barnehama that has raised $66M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 peers—1 public and 8 private companies in the same sector and stage cohort—including Hadrian, Nimble Robotics, Exotec, and Dexterity.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the $66M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.7x multiplier typical for Series C advancement, yielding $112M. The peer-median method examines five robotics companies at Series B, C, and D stages (Exotec at $2.0B, Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B, Dexterity at $1.6B, Hadrian at $1.6B, and Nimble Robotics at $1.0B), producing a median valuation of $1.6B with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B.

The triangulated analysis yields a low estimate of $95M, a median of $881M, and a high of $1.9B. The wide range reflects a meaningful disconnect between the stage-progression method and peer comparables, suggesting material uncertainty around whether Elementary Robotics trades closer to raised-capital norms or peer valuations. Key variables include relative progress on product commercialization, customer traction relative to the peer set, and capital efficiency metrics versus comparable Series C exits.
